summary: Frederick M. Asher was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota, serving from circa 1971 to 2017, including as professor from circa 1985 to 2017.

Frederick M. Smith is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Ludo Rocher. He held positions at the University of Iowa, where he was attested as professor between 2006 and 2008 and as professor emeritus in 2026.

Frederick Price worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at the University of Melbourne, he served in the Madras Civil Service as Chief Secretary to the Government of Madras from 1862 to 1897.

Frederick William Thomas was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Chief Librarian at the India Office (1903-1927) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927-1937).

Frederick Zeuner was an archaeologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Breslau in circa 1928. He worked at the UCL Institute of Archaeology (circa 1936-1963) and as Professor of Environmental Archaeology at the University of London (1946).

Frederik David Kan Bosch was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under Speyer, Uhlenbeck, and Vogel at Leiden. He headed the Archaeological Service in the Netherlands East Indies (1916-1936) and held professorships at Utrecht (1938-1945) and Leiden (1946-1957).

Fredrik Barth studied at the University of Chicago and the University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He held professorships at the University of Bergen (1961-1972), University of Oslo (1974), and Boston University (circa 1997-2008).

Friederike Assandri specializes in Sinology and religious studies, having studied under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer and completed her PhD at Heidelberg University in 2002. She held visiting professorships at Leipzig and Free University of Berlin, working as a Leipzig researcher across 2020-2025.

Friedhelm Hardy specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Paul Hacker, Thomas Burrow, and Robert Charles Zaehner, receiving his degrees from Oxford, and served as Lecturer in Indian Religions at King's College London from circa 1975 to 2004.

Friedrich Adolf Krummacher was a religious studies scholar who studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1785 to 1787. He later held a post at the University of Duisburg from circa 1807 to 1812.

Friedrich Adolf Trendelenburg was a philosopher and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and August Boeckh at Kiel, Leipzig, and Berlin. He spent his academic career at Frederick William University Berlin from circa 1833 to 1872.

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earning doctorates at Paris under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He served as professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1964-1982) and the University of Hamburg (1982-1993).

Friedrich August Rosen was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Bopp, Fleischer, Silvestre de Sacy, and Colebrooke. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages (circa 1828-1831) and Sanskrit (1834) at the University of London.

Friedrich August Wilhelm Krahmer was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. After earning his Ph.D. at the University of Göttingen circa 1830-1833, he served as Privatdozent of Oriental Languages at the University of Marburg from 1833 to 1840.

Friedrich August Wolf was a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne at the University of Göttingen from circa 1777 to 1779 and served at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1783 to 1806.

Friedrich Bechtel was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Benfey, Fick, Bezzenberger, Windisch, and Scherer at Göttingen and Strasbourg. He was a Dozent at Göttingen before serving as ordinary professor at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1895 to 1923.

Friedrich Benedict Weber studied at the University of Leipzig from circa 1792 to 1799. He held posts at European University Viadrina (circa 1802-1811) and the University of Breslau, where he was professor of political economy from circa 1811 to 1848.

Friedrich Bollensen was a linguist and Indologist who studied Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald at Göttingen, earning a Ph.D. circa 1830. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Kazan State University from 1852 to 1856.

Friedrich Brockhaus held professorships at several universities, including the University of Jena (circa 1864-1868), the University of Marburg (circa 1868-1871), the University of Basel (circa 1871-1872), and Kiel University (circa 1872-1895).

Friedrich Carl Andreas was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He studied under Pott, Spiegel, Fleischer, and Benfey, earning a Ph.D. at Erlangen-Nuremberg, and was appointed professor at the University of Göttingen in 1903.
